headline: Sensex drops 548 points as surging oil prices and foreign fund outflows trigger market selloff

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Spike in international oil prices pulled down investor sentiment.
Continued foreign fund outflows put pressure on domestic equities.
Heavy selling was observed in IT, FMCG, PSU Bank, and financial stocks.
Global market cues remained weak amid rising energy costs and restrictive policy signals.
whatHappening: Sensex crashed 548 points while Nifty 50 slipped below the key 22,400 mark to close at 22,363.
ITC and Tech Mahindra were among the top losers, dropping around 3% each.
Polycab is set to exit the F&O segment by Dec. 30, while NCLAT put its insolvency order on hold.
US and Asian markets faced headwinds due to surging crude oil prices ahead of corporate earnings.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices tumbled sharply as Sensex lost 548 points and Nifty fell below 22,400.
The drop was driven by spiking oil prices, foreign fund outflows, and sharp declines in FMCG and IT stocks.
Among individual stocks, ITC and Tech Mahindra dropped 3% each, while Polycab saw NCLAT put its insolvency order on hold.
